title: Extending Equivariant BU to Non-Cyclic Groups: Strategy
content: This file answers the open question from BorsukUlamOQ02OQ01: what happens for non-cyclic groups? The strategy is elegant: rather than computing BU dimensions directly (which requires full equivariant topology), exploit the subgroup monotonicity axiom `buDim_mono` from the parent file. If H ≤ G, then `buDim_H d ≤ buDim_G d`. Both D_n and S_n contain well-understood cyclic subgroups of prime order, and the Yang-Borsuk theorem gives exact values for cyclic prime groups. So: find the prime cyclic subgroups, apply Yang-Borsuk, chain with monotonicity. The axioms in this file (`dihedralBUDim`, `symBUDim`, etc.) encode topological facts — equivariant cohomology calculations — not yet formalized in Mathlib. The theorems prove only the lower bounds derivable from these axioms without further topological input.
mathContext: Strategy: $H \leq G \Rightarrow \text{buDim}(H, d) \leq \text{buDim}(G, d)$. For D_n: $\mathbb{Z}/2 \leq D_n$ and $\mathbb{Z}/p \leq D_n$ for primes $p \mid n$. For S_n: $\mathbb{Z}/p \leq S_n$ for all primes $p \leq n$. Yang-Borsuk: $\text{buDim}(\mathbb{Z}/p, 2k) = 2k-1$ for prime $p$. Combined: $2k-1 \leq \text{buDim}(D_n, 2k)$ and $2k-1 \leq \text{buDim}(S_n, 2k)$ for appropriate primes.

title: Dihedral Group Axioms: Subgroup Structure of D_n
content: The dihedral group D_n is the symmetry group of a regular n-gon: n rotations and n reflections, total order 2n. Three key subgroup facts are axiomatized here: (1) D_n contains Z/2 from the n reflections, each of order 2 (`dihedral_has_Z2`); (2) for any prime p dividing n, the rotation subgroup Z/n ≤ D_n contains a subgroup Z/p (`dihedral_has_rotation_prime`); (3) special cases: D_1 ≅ Z/2 (monogon, just one reflection) and D_2 ≅ Z/2 × Z/2 (Klein four-group: order 4, elements {1, r, s, rs} where r² = s² = 1). The `dihedralBUDim n d : ℕ` itself is axiomatized as a function — its existence is postulated without a construction. This is the correct approach when the function's full computation requires machinery (equivariant cohomology, RO(G)-graded cohomology) not available in Mathlib.
mathContext: $D_n = \langle r, s \mid r^n = s^2 = 1, srs^{-1} = r^{-1} \rangle$, order $2n$. Subgroups: $\langle r \rangle \cong \mathbb{Z}/n$ (rotations); $\langle s \rangle \cong \mathbb{Z}/2$ (one reflection). For prime $p \mid n$: $\langle r^{n/p} \rangle \cong \mathbb{Z}/p \leq \langle r \rangle \leq D_n$. Special cases: $D_1 \cong \mathbb{Z}/2$, $D_2 \cong \mathbb{Z}/2 \times \mathbb{Z}/2$ (Klein four-group).

title: Symmetric Group Axioms: Cyclic Subgroups via p-Cycles
content: The symmetric group S_n (all permutations of n elements, order n!) contains cyclic subgroups of prime order via a simple construction: for any prime p ≤ n, the cyclic permutation (1 2 3 ... p) has order exactly p and generates Z/p ≤ S_n. This is axiomatized as `sym_has_cyclic_prime`. Additionally, fixing one element gives an embedding S_{n-1} ↪ S_n (permutations of the remaining n-1 elements), axiomatized as `sym_has_smaller_sym`. Together these axioms capture: S_n has a rich supply of prime cyclic subgroups (all primes ≤ n), and S_n grows monotonically. The special case S_2 ≅ Z/2 (only two permutations: identity and the transposition) is the base case, exactly matching `buDim 2 d` from the cyclic theory.
mathContext: For prime $p \leq n$: the $p$-cycle $(1 2 \ldots p) \in S_n$ has order $p$, generating $\mathbb{Z}/p \leq S_n$. Subgroup chain: $S_2 \leq S_3 \leq \cdots \leq S_n$ (fix one element). $|S_n| = n!$. Prime factorization of $n!$ includes all primes $\leq n$ (Bertrand's postulate: there is always a prime between $k$ and $2k$, so primes fill densely up to $n$).

title: Dihedral Lower Bounds: Nat.max_le Pattern and Yang-Borsuk
content: The central theorem `dihedralBUDim_odd_prime_lower` establishes `max(buDim 2 d, buDim p d) ≤ dihedralBUDim p d` for prime p. The proof uses `Nat.max_le.mpr ⟨h1, h2⟩`: split the max into two components, prove each separately, then introduce the pair. This `Nat.max_le.mpr` pattern is the idiomatic way to prove max ≤ k goals in Lean 4. The `dihedralBUDim_six_yang_borsuk_bound` instantiates this for D_6 and even-dimensional spaces: since 3 | 6, Z/3 ≤ D_6, so `buDim 3 (2n) = 2n-1 ≤ dihedralBUDim 6 (2n)` by Yang-Borsuk. The rewrite `rw [buDim_prime 3 n (by norm_num) hn]` unpacks the abstract `buDim 3 (2n)` to the concrete value `2n-1`.
mathContext: Yang-Borsuk: $\text{buDim}(\mathbb{Z}/p, 2k) = 2k-1$ for prime $p > 0$. Combined with $\mathbb{Z}/p \leq D_p$: $2k-1 \leq \text{dihedralBUDim}(p, 2k)$. For $D_6$: primes dividing 6 are 2 and 3. From $\mathbb{Z}/3$: $\text{buDim}(3, 2k) = 2k-1 \leq \text{dihedralBUDim}(6, 2k)$. In Lean: `buDim_prime 3 n hp hn : buDim 3 (2 * n) = 2 * n - 1`.

title: S_5 Yang-Borsuk Bound: The Sharpest Lower Bound for S_5
content: For S_5, the sharpest lower bound comes from the prime p = 5 (the largest prime ≤ 5). Since 5 ≤ 5, a 5-cycle generates Z/5 ≤ S_5, and Yang-Borsuk gives `buDim 5 (2n) = 2n-1 ≤ symBUDim 5 (2n)`. The proof of `symBUDim_five_yang_borsuk_bound` applies `sym_has_cyclic_prime 5 (2n) 5` (note the repeated 5: group order 5, prime 5, bound n ≤ 5 = le_rfl) and rewrites with `buDim_prime 5 n`. S_3 is handled separately with both Z/2 and Z/3 bounds, showing that S_3 behaves like D_3 (they are isomorphic: S_3 ≅ D_3, both are the symmetric group of the triangle). For odd-dimensional spaces, the bounds are weaker because `buDim p (2k+1) ≠ 2k` in general — Yang-Borsuk is specific to even-dimensional target spaces when p is an odd prime.
mathContext: For $S_5$: primes $\leq 5$ are 2, 3, 5. Largest prime: 5. Yang-Borsuk: $\text{buDim}(5, 2n) = 2n-1$. So $2n-1 \leq \text{symBUDim}(5, 2n)$. Note $S_3 \cong D_3$: both are generated by a 3-cycle and a transposition. For general $S_n$, the sharpest prime bound is the largest prime $p \leq n$ (by Bertrand's postulate, $p > n/2$, so the bound is within a factor of 2 of optimal).

title: Iterated Monotonicity via Nat Induction: symBUDim_le_of_le
content: The theorem `symBUDim_le_of_le` proves `m ≤ n → symBUDim m d ≤ symBUDim n d` by induction on n. The zero case is immediate (m ≤ 0 implies m = 0, both sides equal). The successor case splits: if m = k+1 then we need `le_refl`, otherwise m < k+1 implies m ≤ k, so we chain the inductive hypothesis `(ih (Nat.lt_succ_iff.mp hlt)).trans (sym_has_smaller_sym (k+1) d ...)`. This `ih.trans h` pattern is the standard Lean 4 way to chain ≤ inequalities: `a ≤ b` and `b ≤ c` combine to `a ≤ c` via `le_trans` or the `.trans` method. The `rcases Nat.eq_or_lt_of_le hmn with rfl | hlt` splits the hypothesis `m ≤ n` into the equal case (rfl: m = n) and strict inequality case.
mathContext: Iterated: $S_m \leq S_{m+1} \leq \cdots \leq S_n$ (subgroup chain via fixing elements). By induction: $\text{symBUDim}(m, d) \leq \text{symBUDim}(m+1, d) \leq \cdots \leq \text{symBUDim}(n, d)$. The key axiom `sym_has_smaller_sym (n d : ℕ) : symBUDim (n-1) d ≤ symBUDim n d` is the single-step case; induction handles the multi-step case.

title: Concrete Instantiations: D_3, D_5, S_4, S_6 Small Cases
content: Part V provides anonymous `example` declarations verifying the framework works for specific small groups. These serve as regression tests: D_3 (= S_3, the symmetry group of an equilateral triangle) gives `n ≤ dihedralBUDim 3 (n+1)` via the Z/2 bound; D_5 (symmetry group of a regular pentagon) gives the Yang-Borsuk bound `2n-1 ≤ dihedralBUDim 5 (2n)` via the Z/5 subgroup; S_4 and S_6 use `sym_has_cyclic_prime` with specific primes (3 for S_4, 5 for S_6); and `symBUDim_le_of_le 2 6 d` shows S_2 ≤ S_6 by the iterated monotonicity theorem. Using `example` (anonymous) rather than `theorem` (named) signals these are illustrative rather than building blocks for further results. In Lean 4, `by norm_num` discharges small arithmetic goals like `3 ≤ 4` automatically.
mathContext: Small group instances: $D_3 \cong S_3$, order 6; $D_5$, order 10; $S_4$, order 24 (contains $\mathbb{Z}/3$ via 3-cycles); $S_6$, order 720 (contains $\mathbb{Z}/5$ via 5-cycles). Monotonicity: $\text{symBUDim}(2, d) \leq \text{symBUDim}(6, d)$ by applying `symBUDim_le_of_le 2 6 d`.
